# Discovery — qualify the use case like a solution architect

You are doing **project discovery** for an agent being built from this factory template.
Behave like an experienced solution architect in a kickoff workshop: **have a conversation**,
don't interrogate. The goal is to understand *what* the builder wants and *whether it's buildable*,
then capture it as the structured spec at `references/context.md`.

## How to run the conversation

- **One topic at a time.** Ask 1–3 focused questions, listen, follow up. Never dump the whole
  checklist at once.
- **Qualify on two tracks in parallel** — *business* (what value, for whom, success looks like) and
  *technical* (what data, tools, systems, constraints make it real).
- **Probe for readiness, not just wishes.** For every capability, ask whether the **data**, **tools/APIs**,
  and **knowledge sources** actually exist today, who owns them, and how the agent would reach them.
- **Reflect back.** Summarize what you heard before moving on, so gaps surface early.
- **Never invent facts.** Anything the builder can't answer becomes a `❓ OPEN` item in the spec.

## If documents were dropped first

If `references/docs/` contains anything beyond its `README.md`, **read it all first** and pre-fill the
spec from it — then use the conversation to confirm and fill gaps, rather than asking what's already written.

## Discovery checklist (what to cover, conversationally)

- **Business**: problem, why now, goals/KPIs, scope and explicit non-goals, stakeholders.
- **Users**: who, technical level, volume, channels (web/devui, Teams, API, voice).
- **Capabilities**: the things the agent should *do*; map each to a candidate `src/skills/<name>/`.
- **Knowledge (RAG)**: which KBs/docs to ground on — format, location, size, freshness, owner.
- **Tools & actions**: external read/write actions; side effects; idempotency.
- **Integrations**: backend systems, protocols (REST/MCP), API contracts, who owns them.
- **Data**: key entities/fields, sample records, PII, retention, residency.
- **Auth & identity**: `DefaultAzureCredential`, managed identity, OBO, RBAC.
- **Non-functional**: latency, availability, scale, accessibility, languages, compliance.

## Always: assess data & tool readiness (platform comes later)

During discovery, focus on **what the agent needs to know and do** — probe the **data**, **tools/APIs**,
and **knowledge sources** behind every capability, and capture their readiness in the spec (§17, §18).
This is what later determines which services the design will call for (e.g. a knowledge base → AI Search,
durable history → Cosmos).

You do **not** confirm the platform here. The builder **consumes** a platform-team-provided environment,
and the exact services are only known once the architecture is designed. So: note in §22 that the
**platform (services) will be confirmed after design**, raise a `❓ OPEN` for anything data/tool-related
that's unclear, and let the `environment-readiness` skill request the concrete service set **after**
`solution-architecture`.

## Output

When the picture is clear enough:

1. **Write `references/context.md`** using the 28-section template below. Keep every heading even if a
   section's body is only `❓ OPEN — <what's missing>`. A visible gap beats a missing section.
2. **Fill `AGENTS.md`** by replacing each `{{MUSTACHE}}` placeholder using the map below. Keep AGENTS.md
   **lean** (one or two lines per placeholder; point to `references/context.md` for detail — never paste
   spec sections in). Delete the top coaching `<!-- … -->` comment block once filled. If a placeholder
   maps only to `❓ OPEN`, leave the placeholder in place so the gap stays visible.
3. **Report back**: what was filled vs. left open, and list every `❓ OPEN` item as numbered follow-up
   questions for the customer/PO.
4. **Hand off**: suggest running the `solution-architecture` skill next to turn the spec into diagrams.

> Confidential material stays in `references/` (gitignored). Never echo secrets into tracked files.

## Template — write this to `references/context.md`

```markdown
# <Project Name> — Project Context

> Structured spec generated by the discovery skill. Source of truth for this project.
> `❓ OPEN` marks facts not yet confirmed — resolve these with the customer.

## A · Identity & Purpose
### 1. Project Overview
Name, one-line purpose, domain, current status.
### 2. Problem Statement & Background
The pain this agent solves; why now.
### 3. Goals & Success Metrics
Measurable outcomes / KPIs that define "done well".
### 4. Scope
In-scope capabilities **and** explicit non-goals.
### 5. Stakeholders & Roles
Customer, sponsor, product owner, dev team, approvers.

## B · Users & Experience
### 6. Primary Users & Personas
Who uses it, technical level, expected volume.
### 7. Channels & Surfaces
Where it runs — devui/web, Teams, API, voice.
### 8. Core User Journeys
The main end-to-end flows, step by step.
### 9. Conversation Design & Persona
Tone, language(s), greeting, fallback / "I don't know" behavior.

## C · Agent Capabilities
### 10. Capabilities & Features
Numbered list of what the agent can do.
### 11. Skills Breakdown
Each capability mapped to a `src/skills/<name>/` (SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/).
### 12. Knowledge Sources
KBs/docs to ground on (RAG) — formats, locations, size, freshness, owner.
### 13. Tools & Actions
External actions it takes (read/write), side effects, idempotency.
### 14. Business Rules & Logic
Routing, prioritization, SLAs, escalation paths, human-in-the-loop.

## D · Integrations & Data
### 15. Systems & Integrations
Backends, protocols (REST/MCP), API contracts, owners.
### 16. Data Model & Entities
Key entities, fields, relationships, sample records.
### 17. Data Handling & Privacy
PII, retention, residency, classification.
### 18. External Dependencies & Assumptions
What must already exist (incl. Azure AI Landing Zone readiness), who provides it, blocking assumptions.

## E · Architecture & Platform
### 19. Solution Architecture
Channels → agent → model → tools/skills → services. (Diagram generated by solution-architecture skill.)
### 20. Model Strategy
Foundry model(s), fallbacks, token/cost considerations.
### 21. Identity & Auth
`DefaultAzureCredential`, managed identity, OBO, RBAC, secret handling.
### 22. Azure Footprint
Foundry Account + Project, Search/Cosmos/monitoring, subscription, region, landing-zone status.
### 23. State & Memory
Conversation history store (file → Cosmos), context providers.

## F · Quality, Ops & Delivery
### 24. Non-Functional Requirements
Latency, availability, scale, accessibility, language support.
### 25. Security & Compliance
Standards, guardrails, content safety, data boundaries.
### 26. Observability & Evaluation
Tracing, logging, eval datasets, monitoring, success thresholds.
### 27. Delivery Plan & Milestones
Prototype → MVP → prod, environments, delivery.
### 28. Open Questions & Risks
Unknowns, pending decisions, risks + mitigations.
```
